procedure.method: Independent review in this fresh session, without spawn, fork, resume, peer reviews or producer explanation. Read the pinned packet, literal case, rules, rubric, compact method/addendum and adapter. Read all five pinned native-evidence manifests before poster opening; did not follow their unlisted embedded paths. The packet explicitly has no source assets and no protected-layout manifests. Opened and visually inspected the exact pinned PNGs through functions.exec calling tools.view_image with detail original, sequentially M1 native/usage720/thumbnail320, then M2, M3, M4 and M5 in that same three-view order. All fifteen image outputs were displayed before the deliberate first copy-reading/transcription stage, any mandatory judgment or any score. First readings below were made from those displayed pixels after the complete viewing pass, not supplied-copy fallback. No ambiguity-triggered revisit, crop, OCR, replacement asset, image edit or generation was used. File hash/byte checks and PNG-header dimensions corroborate bindings but are not claimed as visual opens. Session identity is unavailable here and remains null.

Every practical line is readable with strong dark-on-cream contrast. Lower groups are smaller than the schedule but retain adequate weight and separation.

The clean vertical boundary keeps busy river reflections and attendees from interfering with the information; the photo has enough room for screen and audience.
Concrete, reflected lamps, layered winter clothing and patterned mats form a coherent photographic environment. Screen frame and support legs are legible.
A landscape image on the screen and the adjacent microphone speaker preserve both cinematic and social actions, with no prominent malformed local object visible.
seated adults and evening river lights
Warm lights against blue evening water create a relaxed neighborhood-cinema feeling with adult attendees rather than a childish or extravagant spectacle.
The modest speaker scale and informal mats communicate approachable participation.
No stray lettering, decorative filler, logo or watermark is visible. Screen, bridge, crowd and practical text have clear functional roles.
Visible clothing silhouettes and supports are coherent enough for close inspection; the scenic movie image remains a broad cinema cue rather than a specific short-film identity.

residuals: The screen carries a generic scenic landscape rather than a distinctive short-film moment; the screening action itself is clear.
The image/sidebar arrangement and heavy sans treatment are familiar event-signage devices. They are resolved here but do not reach exceptional formal specificity.

The river provides a central channel of visual space and the bridge separates, then links, the two activity groups. Text is placed in open banks rather than pasted over people.
Information groups occupy distinct areas without clipping the illustration or crowding the margins; the eye travels between them instead of meeting one uniform sidebar.
bridge railing, piers, rocks and foliage
The drawn environment has consistent linework, limited shading and a controlled peach/navy/gold palette. Bridge supports and railings retain a recognizable spatial structure.
People, chairs, mats and the microphone gesture are coherent at the chosen illustrative scale; figure simplification matches the broader environment.

The overhead distance and warm ground produce a calm, sociable community atmosphere; seated adults and the speaker keep it appropriate to an adult cultural event.

The modest moonlit screen image and vegetation support a gentle cinema mood without cartoon mascots or excessive spectacle.
No arbitrary symbol, stray text or fake map legend is added. The detailed bridge, screen, seating and river relate to the requested event.
The figures are simplified rather than anatomically elaborate, and their scale is consistent. The dense vegetation is decorative but remains subordinate to the two actions and text.

evidence: A close audience-level photograph carries the title and scene across the left two-thirds; consolidated practical groups occupy the right. Its informational split differs from the other four organizations.

A speaking/listening portrait relationship is the main emotional image; angled upper-left and lower-right panels frame a small lower cinema scene. This has different image dominance and information structure from M4 despite a closely related palette and grain.
diagonal bridge, river and two scene groups

An overhead illustration turns the bridge into a compositional connector between screening and talk. Distributed terrain text pockets and small figures create an overview unlike the four closer photographic constructions.
projector beam and large information screen

A large foreground machine and diagonal beam organize the poster; schedule and participation copy inhabit the depicted cinema screen. This integration of text into the scene differs from M2’s exterior collage panels and from M1/M5’s information columns.
schedule-led left block and right title/vignette

Date/time dominate the left, the identity is a separate upper-right block, and the bridge-shaped photographic cutout fills the lower right. It shares photographic realism and heavy type with M1, but changes hierarchy, cropping boundary and the relationship between image and information.
relationship to M4 and quieter M1/M5

M2 foregrounds warm interpersonal faces, M4 foregrounds the spectacle of projection, M1/M5 foreground practical invitation and venue, and M3 offers a calm illustrated overview. These different focal mechanisms and emotional emphasis support a strong but not exceptional five-direction set.
typography and screen imagery across all five

All five rely on very heavy Hangul sans and uppercase English, and M1/M2/M4/M5 repeat riverside screen imagery with scenic film content. Formal range is therefore limited despite substantive differences in composition, viewpoint and image/type roles.
residuals: The typography remains in a narrow heavy-sans family across all five. There is no five-way range of type voices.

M2/M4 share purple/coral/lime and grain; M1/M5 share a relatively neutral photographic information format. Their separation rests on actual composition and image/type roles, not on material names alone.

Riverside architecture, seated audiences and scenic images on screens recur across the set. The common venue supports the brief, but the repeated generalized film imagery limits exceptional portfolio specificity.
This is one independent portfolio review of the exact initial packet. It does not assert the combined result of three critics or readability on a physical station display.
